sources.citation: Vyas, Yogendra D. 1967. A linguistic study of Bhili dialects: a descriptive study of Central and North Bhili. PhD thesis, Gujarat University (Shodhganga 10603/49002).
sources.note: 'Stress is not distinctive. Syllable division can be made in terms of phonetic criteria.' (thesis p.28) -- but this is Central Bhili of Sukhsar, Panchmahals (bhil1251), a different Bhil variety; not usable for dung1251.

sources.citation: Grierson, George A. (ed.). 1907. Linguistic Survey of India, Vol. IX, Part III: Indo-Aryan family, Central group, The Bhil languages, including Khandesi, Banjari or Labhani, Bahrupia, &c. Calcutta: Office of the Superintendent of Government Printing. (archive.org in.ernet.dli.2015.34952 scanned text)
sources.note: Nothing. The sections nearest Dungra Bhil territory (Nori of Ali Rajpur pp.105-106; Bhili of Ali Rajpur, Rajpipla, Chhota Udepur/Rewakantha remarks; Pawri) give only segmental pronunciation notes (a>o, r-dropping, deaspiration, nasalisation). Whole-volume grep for accent/stress/tone hits only the front-matter transcription convention ('When it is necessary to mark an accented syllable, the acute accent is used'). No 'Dungri/Dungra' section exists.
